zh: 没有必要先用小锤敲几下再用大锤：直接用大锤一次击碎更省。因此每块砖要么完全交给大锤（花 1 次），要么完全交给小锤（花 strength 次）。
先假设全部用小锤，总数为 Σstrength；把第 i 块改用大锤能节省 strength[i]−1 次。在至多 k 块的额度内应优先挑节省最多的，也就是强度最大的砖；强度为 1 的砖节省 0，用哪种锤都一样。
把强度大于 1 的砖按强度降序排序，取前 min(k, 个数) 块标记为大锤；再按下标从小到大扫描，被标记的放进大锤组、其余放进小锤组；总击数 = 大锤组大小 + 小锤组强度之和（用 64 位整数）；按三行输出，某组为空就输出 -1。
en: There is no point hitting a brick with the small hammer first and then using the big hammer: one big-hammer hit alone is cheaper. So each brick goes entirely to the big hammer (1 hit) or entirely to the small hammer (strength hits).

Start from using the small hammer everywhere, which costs the sum of all strengths; moving brick i to the big hammer saves strength[i]-1 hits. Within the quota of at most k bricks prefer the largest savings, i.e. the strongest bricks; a brick of strength 1 saves nothing, so either hammer is fine for it.

Sort the bricks with strength greater than 1 by strength in descending order and mark the first min(k, count) for the big hammer; then scan indices in increasing order, putting marked bricks in the big-hammer group and the rest in the small-hammer group; the total is the big group's size plus the small group's strength sum (64-bit); print three lines, using -1 for an empty group.
ja: レンガをまず小ハンマーで叩いてから大ハンマーを使う意味はありません。大ハンマーの 1 回の打撃だけのほうが安いからです。したがって、各レンガは完全に大ハンマー (1 回) か、完全に小ハンマー (strength 回) のどちらかに割り当てます。
すべて小ハンマーで割る場合から始めると、コストはすべての強さの合計です。レンガ i を大ハンマーに移すと、strength[i]-1 回節約できます。最大 k 個という上限の範囲で、節約量が最大のもの、つまり最も強いレンガを優先します。強さ 1 のレンガは何も節約できないので、どちらのハンマーでも構いません。
強さが 1 より大きいレンガを強さの降順にソートし、先頭の min(k, 個数) 個を大ハンマーとしてマークします。次にインデックスの昇順に走査して、マークされたレンガを大ハンマーのグループ、それ以外を小ハンマーのグループに入れます。合計は大ハンマーのグループの大きさと小ハンマーのグループの強さの合計 (64 ビット) の和です。3 行を出力し、空のグループには -1 を使います。
ko: 작은 망치로 먼저 친 뒤 큰 망치를 쓰는 것은 의미가 없습니다. 큰 망치 한 번만 쓰는 편이 더 저렴하기 때문입니다. 따라서 각 벽돌은 전부 큰 망치(1번)로 부수거나, 전부 작은 망치(strength번)로 부숩니다.
모든 벽돌에 작은 망치를 쓰는 경우에서 시작하면 비용은 강도의 합입니다. 벽돌 i를 큰 망치로 옮기면 strength[i]-1번을 절약합니다. 최대 k개라는 제한 안에서 절약량이 가장 큰 벽돌, 즉 가장 강한 벽돌을 우선 고릅니다. 강도 1인 벽돌은 절약되는 것이 없으므로 어느 망치를 써도 됩니다.
강도가 1보다 큰 벽돌을 강도 내림차순으로 정렬하고, 앞에서부터 min(k, 개수)개를 큰 망치로 표시합니다. 그다음 번호를 오름차순으로 훑으며 표시된 벽돌은 큰 망치 그룹에, 나머지는 작은 망치 그룹에 넣습니다. 총합은 큰 그룹의 크기와 작은 그룹의 강도 합(64비트)을 더한 값입니다. 세 줄을 출력하되 빈 그룹은 -1로 출력합니다.
vi: Không có ích gì khi đập viên gạch bằng búa nhỏ trước rồi mới dùng búa lớn: một lần đập của búa lớn đã rẻ hơn. Vì vậy mỗi viên gạch hoặc giao hoàn toàn cho búa lớn (1 lần đập) hoặc giao hoàn toàn cho búa nhỏ (strength lần đập).

Bắt đầu từ việc dùng búa nhỏ cho tất cả, tốn tổng các strength; chuyển viên gạch i sang búa lớn tiết kiệm được strength[i]-1 lần đập. Trong hạn mức tối đa k viên, ưu tiên các mức tiết kiệm lớn nhất, tức là các viên gạch cứng nhất; viên gạch strength 1 không tiết kiệm gì nên búa nào cũng được.

Sắp xếp các viên gạch có strength lớn hơn 1 theo strength giảm dần và đánh dấu min(k, số lượng) viên đầu cho búa lớn; sau đó duyệt các chỉ số theo thứ tự tăng, đưa viên đã đánh dấu vào nhóm búa lớn và các viên còn lại vào nhóm búa nhỏ; tổng bằng kích thước nhóm lớn cộng tổng strength của nhóm nhỏ (64 bit); in ba dòng, dùng -1 cho nhóm rỗng.

explanationEn:
## Fixed source and conventions

fastprep/Wayfair/wayfair-smash-the-bricks.md at fixed commit e66f809f4c953bce129f68491726176615db6afc states explicitly: n≤200000, 0≤bigHits≤200000, and the strengths are distinct integers in 1..10^9; the number of big-hammer uses is the maximum blows, i.e. at most rather than exactly. Positions are numbered from 1, each of the two index groups is in ascending order, and an unused hammer corresponds to [-1]. In original example 3, bigHits=9 and n=8, which explicitly allows a quota larger than the number of bricks.

This site lays out the original returned 2D array [[total],[big indices],[small indices]] as exactly three lines, without adding an element count to any line; an unused group is written as -1. A brick of strength 1 may use either hammer as long as the result is still optimal and within the quota; no extra tie-breaking rule is imposed. All four original examples are kept. Both the original return description and the starter explicitly use a long 2D array; the total number of hits over the full range can exceed 32 bits, so this site uses 64 bits. The missing hammer durability and operation order cited by the old blocked note do not match the fixed raw file: there is only a maximum number of big-hammer uses, and no durability decay is defined. One place in the explanation of original example 2 miswrites the big-hammer indices as [3,5,7], but the official output of the same example and the end of its explanation both give [3,5,6,7], consistent with the total of 13 hits; this site keeps the correct complete list and discloses the missing index. The mathematical core of the algorithm reuses this site's already verified implementation of the same rules, but this problem is bound independently to the Wayfair source, and all data were regenerated with new seeds and a new dynamic-programming oracle. No upstream code was executed.

## Approach

First assume every brick uses the small hammer, for a total of Σstrength[i] hits. Switching brick i to the big hammer takes only 1 hit, saving strength[i]−1 hits. It is enough to choose at most k of the largest positive savings; the reference program only selects bricks with strength greater than 1, sorts them by strength in descending order and takes the first k, and finally outputs the indices of the two groups in their original order. A brick of strength 1 saves 0; the reference program does not choose it, but choosing it or not can both be optimal, and the semantic checker accepts every equivalent grouping.

## Proof of correctness

No optimal strategy needs to hit a brick a few times with the small hammer and then break it with the big hammer: after removing the earlier small-hammer hits, the big hammer still breaks it in one hit, at lower cost. Hitting the same brick with the big hammer more than once is also pointless. Hence there is an optimal strategy that assigns each brick entirely to one hammer. A brick assigned to the big hammer costs 1, otherwise its original strength; the costs of the bricks add up, and at most k bricks go to the big hammer.

For any chosen set, if a chosen brick's saving is smaller than some unchosen brick's saving, swapping the two keeps the number of big-hammer uses and lowers the total number of hits. So maximizing the total saving means preferring the largest savings. While quota remains, adding any positive saving strictly improves the cost, until the quota is used up or all positive savings are chosen; the only possible zero saving does not change the cost whether it is chosen or not. The reference choice therefore achieves the global minimum total number of hits. The two output groups form a disjoint partition of all indices, each generated by scanning the indices in order, which meets the ascending and 1-based requirements.

## Complexity and full bounds

Sorting is O(n log n), building the groups is O(n), and space is O(n). The largest valid sum of distinct strengths is 200000×(2×10^9−200000+1)/2=199980000100000, so 64-bit integers should be used; Python integers are safe. The algorithm does not simulate hits one by one, so strengths of 10^9 and two hundred thousand bricks are handled directly.

## Independent verification and semantic checking

The small oracle runs a quota dynamic program brick by brick, whose state is the processed prefix and the number of big-hammer uses so far, with transitions for the small-hammer cost strength[i] and the big-hammer cost 1, keeping a witness of the optimal grouping; it does not use the sorted-saving formula and does not read any other problem's expected files. All 163 unique inputs go through the real reference subprocess, and the results are checked by total cost and validity of the grouping, not compared token by token with the oracle's index sequence.

The checker requires exactly three lines, verifies ascending indices, a disjoint and complete partition, the quota and the cost, and then compares the optimal total. In particular, for n=1,k=1,strength=[1] both "1 / 1 / -1" and "1 / -1 / 1" must pass; for the full 1..200000 with k=200000, two optimal witnesses that give the strength-1 brick to different hammers are also covered. The full large bounds include k=0, k=n, k>n, half quota, shuffled order and 64-bit totals. The two negative controls choose the weakest bricks and overflow the total cost in 32 bits, respectively; each must exit normally to count as a valid counterexample.
